To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a new knowledge-based statistical approach can be used to identify active scaffolds with valuable SAR information from uHTS data, and it can greatly improve the confirmation rate compared to a standard threshold-based approach.

the "top X" screening hit selection method, currently widely used in HTS data analysis, is not effective in identifying good-quality hits; a novel knowledge-based approach, driven by hidden SAR information within a screening library and using a statistical model, can be used to directly identify active scaffolding containing valuable SAR information, with a greatly improved hit confirmation rate (from 55 to 85%); this approach may help to produce high-quality leads for drug discovery.

the standard "top-X" approach for primary hit selection is not effective and that a novel knowledge-based approach can directly identify active chemical scaffolds with good structure-activity relationships.
